PHILADELPHIA, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Board of Trustees of Aberdeen Multi-Market Income Fund (NYSE: MMT) has approved a 1-for-4 reverse stock split of the Fund's issued and outstanding common shares, effective prior to the opening of trading on November 9, 2026.

The Board approved the reverse stock split to increase the Fund's per-share market price. The Board believes a higher share price may reduce certain trading and administrative frictions associated with lower-priced securities, increase the Fund's suitability for certain investment platforms and intermediary programs, and better align the Fund's share price with industry trading conventions.

The aggregate value of a shareholder's investment is not expected to change solely as a result of the reverse stock split, although the market value of Fund shares will continue to fluctuate based on market conditions.

Under the terms of the transaction, every four common shares will be consolidated into one common share. No fractional shares will be issued; fractional share entitlements will be aggregated and sold, with the net proceeds distributed to affected shareholders. The transaction will apply equally to all shareholders and will not affect any shareholder's proportionate ownership interest, other than minor adjustments resulting from the treatment of fractional shares.

Following the transaction, the Fund's common shares will continue to trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol MMT. A new CUSIP number will be assigned to the Fund.

The reverse stock split will not alter the Fund's managed distribution policy. The Fund will continue to pay monthly distributions at an annualized rate equal to 11.00% of the Fund's average daily net asset value for the previous month-end prior to the declaration date. The percentage of net asset value used to determine distributions will remain unchanged following the reverse stock split. However, because fewer shares will be outstanding following the reverse stock split, the distribution paid on a per-share basis is expected to increase proportionately, while the overall distribution rate remains unchanged.

Shareholders holding shares through a brokerage account will generally have their holdings adjusted automatically. Shareholders holding physical share certificates or those with questions regarding their account should contact the Fund's transfer agent, Computershare Trust Company, N.A. Please refer to the contact details at the end of this release.

Important Information

Shares of closed-end funds are listed for trading on national securities exchanges and are bought and sold in the secondary market. The market price of a fund's shares is determined by supply and demand and may be greater than (a "premium") or less than (a "discount") the fund's net asset value (NAV). A fund's investment return and principal value will fluctuate, and investors may receive more or less than their original investment upon the sale of shares. There is no assurance that a fund will achieve its investment objective. Past performance is not indicative of future results.

The trading price of a closed-end fund's shares may be influenced by various factors, including market conditions, investor sentiment, and other external forces, and is not directly controlled by the fund, its Board of Trustees, or its investment adviser. As a result, shares may trade at a premium to or discount from NAV at any given time. A premium to NAV may not be sustained, and a discount to NAV may increase or decrease over time. Investors should consider these risks when purchasing or selling closed-end fund shares.

Shareholders whose fund shares trade at a premium to NAV and who participate in the fund's dividend reinvestment plan should be aware that distributions may be reinvested at prices above NAV, which may adversely affect investment results.

About Aberdeen Investments

Aberdeen Investments Global is the trade name of Aberdeen's investments business, herein referred to as "Aberdeen Investments" or "Aberdeen". In the United States, Aberdeen Investments refers to the following affiliated, registered investment advisers: abrdn Inc., abrdn Investments Limited, and abrdn Asia Limited.

Aberdeen Investments is among the world's largest asset managers, with decades of experience overseeing closed-end funds dating back to the 1980s. As of June 30, 2026, the firm had approximately $527 billion in assets under management. Closed-end funds represent a core component of Aberdeen Investments' client franchise in both the U.S. and global markets. Initiative enables suppliers through renewable energy aggregation and supplier capability building

LAUSANNE, Switzerland & SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Logitech International (SIX: LOGN) (Nasdaq: LOGI) today announced the launch of Chain Reaction, a global supply chain decarbonization program designed to help supply partners cut carbon emissions, optimize factory operations and unlock shared business growth. The initiative marks an expansion of Logitech’s climate strategy, providing direct operational support to help suppliers build their own decarbonization roadmaps while advancing Logitech’s science-based target to halve its Scope 3 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 2030.

Core Pillars of Chain Reaction

Launching with an initial cohort of 17 key suppliers, Chain Reaction delivers collaborative enablement across four pillars:

  • Affordable clean energy: Convenes suppliers to aggregate purchasing power and collectively procure high-standard renewable energy instruments. This secures clean electricity at competitive pricing, mitigating long-term volatility and energy risk.
  • Energy and greenhouse gas evaluations: Supports supplier-led factory evaluations to identify energy, thermal and mechanical efficiencies. This empowers suppliers to define reduction targets and roadmaps that serve their entire customer base.
  • Expert support and guidance: Provides technical workshops, roundtables and innovation sessions, alongside co-developed reporting tools. These are designed to streamline carbon accounting and eliminate administrative overhead.
  • Commercial recognition: Integrates carbon transparency and decarbonization into regular business reviews and new business awards, ensuring manufacturing partners gain executive visibility and recognition for measurable carbon reductions.

In fiscal year 2026, Logitech already achieved a 33% reduction in its total Scope 3 carbon footprint compared to its 2021 baseline1. Chain Reaction builds on this momentum by empowering suppliers to identify carbon hotspots and execute practical engineering solutions directly within their facilities and supply chains.

“Real value-chain decarbonization happens directly on the factory floor,” said Elaine Laird, chief people and sustainability officer at Logitech. “Our suppliers understand their operations best. Chain Reaction helps our manufacturing partners access the practical tools, technical evaluations and clean energy solutions they need to optimize their operations and lead their own decarbonization roadmaps.”

To support participating facilities, the program provides technical workshops on establishing GHG baselines, direct access to subject matter experts and pathways to pilot cutting-edge innovations through the Logitech Future Positive Challenge.

“By integrating carbon transparency and decarbonization progress into our commercial metrics, we are enabling more value for our suppliers to grow with Logitech,” said Sree Chenincherry, chief supply chain operations officer at Logitech. “From an operational standpoint, decarbonization and efficiency go hand-in-hand. Equipping our manufacturing partners to reduce energy waste and transition to clean power unlocks structural cost savings, mitigates long-term volatility and strengthens our entire shared value chain.”

About Logitech

Logitech creates design-led, software-enabled hardware solutions that help businesses thrive and bring people together when working, creating and gaming in the age of AI. As the point of connection between people and the digital world, our mission is to extend human potential in work and play, in a way that is good for people and the planet. Founded in 1981, Logitech International is a Swiss public company listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (LOGN) and on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (LOGI). Find Logitech and its other brands, including Logitech G, at www.logitech.com or company blog.

Logitech and other Logitech marks are trademarks or registered trademarks of Logitech Europe S.A. and/or its affiliates in the U.S. and other countries. All other trademarks are the property of their respective owners. For more information about Logitech and its products, visit the company’s website at www.logitech.com.

Key Terms

scope 3technical
Scope 3 describes all greenhouse gas emissions that occur upstream and downstream of a company’s direct operations—things like emissions from suppliers, transportation, product use, and disposal. Think of it as the hidden carbon footprint tied to everything a business buys, sells, or enables; it matters to investors because these indirect emissions can drive regulatory costs, supply-chain disruption, consumer preference shifts, and long-term valuation risk that aren’t visible on a company’s factory floor or utility bill.
ghgtechnical
Greenhouse gases (GHGs) are air pollutants like carbon dioxide and methane that trap heat in the atmosphere, similar to how a blanket holds in body warmth. For investors, GHGs matter because companies' emissions affect regulatory costs, reputational risk, and long-term business viability as governments and consumers push for lower emissions; measuring and reducing GHGs can signal future compliance, efficiency gains, or potential liabilities.

HONG KONG, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- 3 E Network Technology Group Limited (Nasdaq: MASK) (the “Company” or “3e Network”), a business-to-business (“B2B”) information technology (“IT”) business solutions provider, today announced that the Company’s board of directors approved on October 10, 2026 that the Company’s Class A ordinary shares (the “Class A Ordinary Shares”) and Class B ordinary shares (the “Class B Ordinary Shares”) be consolidated on a 2 for 1 ratio with the marketplace effective date of October 30, 2026.

Beginning with the opening of trading on October 30, 2026, the Company’s Class A Ordinary Shares will trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market on a split-adjusted basis, under the same symbol “MASK” but under a new CUSIP Number, G8849D136.

As a result of the share consolidation, each two (2) ordinary shares outstanding will automatically combine and convert to one (1) issued and outstanding ordinary share without any action on the part of the shareholders. No fractional shares will be issued to any shareholders in connection with the share consolidation, and any fractional shares which would have resulted from the share consolidation will be rounded up to the next whole number.

Revenue

Staff costs for the six months ended April 30, 2026 decreased to US$5.6 million, compared to US$8.6 million in the comparable period in 2025, reflecting optimized operational efficiencies across the Group.

Depreciation and Amortization

Depreciation and amortization for the six months ended April 30, 2026 increased to US$5.0 million, compared to US$4.7 million in the same period in the prior year. This increase is primarily attributable to the addition of the New York hotel property to our real estate portfolio.

Finance Costs

Finance costs for the six months ended April 30, 2026 decreased by 24.9% to US$4.6 million, compared to US$6.1 million in the comparable period in 2025.

Other Expenses

Other expenses for the six months ended April 30, 2026 increased to US$13.0 million, compared to US$11.0 million in the comparable period in 2025. Other income increased to US$12.5 million for the six months ended April 30, 2026, compared to US$10.7 million for the comparable period in 2025, mainly due to higher interest income driven by an increase in outstanding balances owed by group companies during the current period.

Profit for the six months ended April 30, 2026 was US$42.4 million, compared to US$51.5 million in the comparable period in 2025. An accounting category for investments and contracts that are updated to their current market price on the balance sheet, with any gain or loss immediately shown in the company’s profit or loss statement. earnings per sharefinancial
Earnings per share represent the amount of profit a company makes for each share of its stock, similar to how a pie’s total size can be divided into slices for each person. It helps investors understand how profitable the company is on a per-share basis, making it easier to compare its performance over time or against other companies. non-controlling interestsfinancial

Property, plant and equipment are a company’s long-term physical assets—land, buildings, factories, machinery, vehicles and similar items—used in day-to-day operations rather than held for sale. Ifetroban was well tolerated in patients with systemic sclerosis

NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cumberland Pharmaceuticals Inc. (NASDAQ: CPIX), an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company advancing new therapies that address significant unmet medical needs, announces top-line results from its Phase 2a ASSIST-SSc trial evaluating oral ifetroban for patients with systemic sclerosis ("SSc"). These results support the safety and tolerability of ifetroban in this rare disease population. Cumberland will next complete correlative biomarker studies using specimens collected during the trial, along with an evaluation of cardiac imaging from patients continuing on the open-label extension.

SSc is a rare autoimmune disease characterized by excess collagen deposition resulting in skin thickening, cardiovascular disease, gastrointestinal problems, and more, and affects approximately 100,000 individuals in the U.S. Current therapies target specific manifestations of SSc, and approved options are available for SSc-associated interstitial lung disease. However, there is no approved therapy directed at the primary cardiac issues associated with SSc. Both cardiac and pulmonary manifestations remain among the leading causes of mortality for patients with the disease.

Ifetroban is a once-daily oral medication that works by blocking the thromboxane receptor, which plays a key role in inflammation, vascular dysfunction and fibrosis. In preclinical models of pulmonary arterial hypertension and heart disease, ifetroban treatment was associated with a reduction in fibrosis and provided cardioprotective effects (West 2016). A delay or inhibition of tissue fibrosis and improved cardiac function could provide significant improvement in quality of life for SSc patients. These preclinical results were foundational to the development of this Phase 2a clinical trial.

The 12-month Phase 2a ASSIST-SSc trial (NCT02682511) was a pilot trial to evaluate the safety of oral ifetroban in patients with SSc. Patients with either diffuse cutaneous (dcSSc) or pulmonary arterial hypertension (SSc-PAH) manifestations were randomized to receive ifetroban or matching placebo. A total of 31 subjects received ifetroban (22 dcSSc and 9 SSc-PAH) and 10 subjects received placebo (9 dcSSc and 1 SSc-PAH). Safety was evaluated by the frequency of treatment emergent adverse events between treatment groups. Exploratory efficacy endpoints were evaluated by SSc cohort to assess the effect of ifetroban on multiple aspects of SSc disease, including cardiovascular, pulmonary, skin, activity and quality of life.

Ifetroban was generally well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with prior experience. As in prior ifetroban studies, gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent in the ifetroban group than in the placebo group; the majority were mild and resolved. A modest increase in bleeding-related adverse events was also observed with ifetroban, in keeping with its mechanism as a thromboxane prostanoid receptor antagonist, and these events were predominantly mild. No serious adverse event during the 12-month treatment period was assessed by the medical monitor as related to study drug.

The majority of subjects in both treatment groups showed limited disease progression during the study, which reduced the ability of a trial of this size to detect a treatment difference. This Phase 2a trial was not designed or powered to evaluate efficacy, and the sample size and exploratory analytic approach preclude efficacy conclusions.

Cumberland has reviewed the results from both the dcSSc and SSc-PAH cohorts with clinical experts in SSc. As next steps, the Company plans to submit the clinical study report to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") and to also complete correlative biomarker studies using specimens collected during the trial, along with an evaluation of cardiac imaging from patients continuing on the open-label extension. Those findings will inform Cumberland's decision on the further development of ifetroban in SSc.

About Systemic Sclerosis (SSc)

SSc is a rare autoimmune connective tissue disease which is characterized by rapidly progressing fibrosis and atrophy in the musculoskeletal system and internal organs including the lungs, heart, gastrointestinal tract and kidneys. While approved therapies exist for certain pulmonary manifestations, no therapy is currently approved to treat or prevent the primary cardiac involvement of SSc.

Cumberland Pharmaceuticals Inc. is an innovation-focused biopharmaceutical company developing new therapies to address significant unmet medical needs and improve the quality of patient care. The Company is advancing a clinical pipeline of late-stage product candidates across multiple therapeutic areas with significant unmet medical needs.

Cumberland's Phase 2 clinical programs are also evaluating ifetroban in patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis and Cancer Metastasis.

SACRAMENTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--River City Bank (Nasdaq: RCBC) ("the Bank") reported net income of $30.6 million or $2.16 per share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, which compares to $19.7 million, or $1.36 per share, for the same period in 2025. Net income was $68.2 million or $4.75 per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, which compares to $47.4 million, or $3.24 per share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The Bank’s earnings for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 resulted in a 21.06% return on average equity and a 1.92% return on average assets. The Bank’s book value per share rose 14% to $42.32 as of September 30, 2026 from $37.04 per share as of September 30, 2025.

In August 2026, the Bank successfully completed its initial public offering (“IPO”) and its shares began trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the RCBC ticker symbol. The secondary offering consisted solely of existing shares held by two of the Bank's long-time shareholders associated with the family of the Bank's founder, Jon Kelly, and no new shares were issued by the Bank. The IPO was a major milestone in the Bank's history, increased the Bank's visibility within the public capital markets, and provided liquidity for shareholders, while establishing a publicly traded market value for its common stock.

  • Net income increased to $30.6 million, or $2.16 per share, for the third quarter of 2026, as compared to $19.6 million, or $1.37 per share, for the preceding quarter and $19.7 million, or $1.36 per share, for the same period in the prior year. This significant increase in the current quarter was primarily due to a $17.1 million mark-to-market (“MTM”) gain related to certain interest rate swaps. The MTM gain was due to the increase in U.S. Treasury rates during the third quarter of 2026. Management believes that core PTPP income(1), which also removes the MTM gains and losses is a better metric to evaluate the Bank's core earnings. Core PTPP income increased 15% to $29.3 million for the third quarter of 2026 as compared to $25.4 million for the trailing quarter and increased 3% from $28.4 million for the same quarter in the prior year.
  • Average loans increased by $108 million (2% growth) compared to the trailing quarter and by $363 million (8% growth) compared to the same period in the prior year, reflecting continued organic loan growth.
  • Average deposits for the third quarter of 2026 increased by $158 million (3% growth) compared to the trailing quarter and by $766 million (16% growth) compared to the same period in the prior year, supporting the Bank’s loan growth and liquidity position.
  • As of September 30, 2026, the Bank had zero non-performing loans, virtually no delinquent loans (0.00% of total loans), no loans more than 90 days past due and still accruing interest, no other real estate owned (“OREO”), and the Bank’s Allowance for Credit Losses for Loans (“ACL”) was 2.30% of total loans. Due to the loan growth, the Bank recorded a $3.7 million provision for credit losses (loans and unfunded commitments) for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.5 million provision in the trailing quarter and a $644,000 reversal of provision for the same period in the prior year. The ACL to total loans ratio was unchanged at September 30, 2026 from the prior quarter end at 2.30%.
  • The Bank continued to maintain an exceptional efficiency ratio by industry standards at 19.4% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 29.4% in both the trailing quarter and the third quarter of 2025. Even excluding the $17.1 million MTM gain on undesignated interest rate swaps, the Bank's adjusted efficiency ratio(1) was 27.7% compared to 31.9% in the trailing quarter and 28.2% for the same period in the prior year.
  • Net interest margin (“NIM”) – The Bank’s NIM was 2.39% and 2.34% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026. “This quarter was quite exceptional in the Bank’s 53-year history due to our IPO and listing on the Nasdaq. We believe that becoming a public company will enable us to further enhance shareholder value, which has always been management's and the Board's “North Star”. The Bank also delivered solid core operating results in the third quarter of 2026, as evidenced by the operating metrics and continued compounding of book value per share,” said Steve Fleming, President and Chief Executive Officer. “In addition, the Bank grew loans by 3.7% over the prior quarter-end and credit quality remains pristine as we have not suffered any material losses on loans originated since the current management team took over in 2008.”

Mr. Fleming also noted, “The Bank recognized a $17.1 million MTM gain related to its undesignated interest rate swaps. The Bank systematically enters interest rate swaps to mitigate interest rate risk and all swaps are entered into for economic and risk management purposes (regardless of accounting treatment). Approximately 16% of the Bank’s interest rate swaps are undesignated as of September 30, 2026, and until these interest rate swaps are designated as a hedge to specific assets or liabilities, the MTM fluctuations (positive and negative) will flow through the income statement.” Given the hedging purpose of the swaps, Bank management does not view the MTM gains and losses to be indicative of the Bank's core operating performance. As such, for the purposes of disclosure in this earnings release, the Bank has shown several important metrics which remove this non-core component of net income such as earnings per share, return on average equity, return on average asset, and operating efficiency.

Brian Killeen, Chief Financial Officer said, “The Bank continues to perform at a high level, as reflected in the following key metrics: return on average equity, return on average assets, and operating efficiency. We view operational efficiency as a competitive advantage, contributing to sustained profitability and growth in shareholder value. Despite the increase in U.S. Treasury rates during the current quarter, the Bank’s high quality, short duration investment securities portfolio continued to perform well with a relatively low unrealized loss position of 1.5% as of September 30, 2026.”

In addition to results presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America (GAAP), this press release contains non-GAAP financial measures. Management has presented these non-GAAP financial measures in this press release because management believes that they provide useful and comparative information to assess trends in the Bank's core operations. However, the non-GAAP financial measures are supplemental and are not a substitute for any analysis based on GAAP. Where applicable, comparable earnings information using GAAP financial measures is also presented. Core Pre-Tax, Pre-Provision Income

This figure is defined as net interest income, plus noninterest income, less the change in the fair value of derivatives, less noninterest expense. The purpose of this non-GAAP financial measure is to remove the market volatility that can be included in the change in the fair value of derivatives that do not have fair value hedge accounting treatment (undesignated), which is a component of noninterest income. We hedge our interest rate risk through interest rate derivatives and a portion of the gain/loss on derivatives is reflected in our income statement. In addition, this measure is shown before the provision for credit losses and income tax expense. We believe that this non-GAAP financial measure provides a clearer picture of our operational earnings.

Key Terms

mark-to-marketfinancial
"Mark-to-market" is a method of valuing assets or investments based on their current market price, rather than their original cost or value. It helps investors see the most up-to-date worth of their holdings, much like checking the latest price of a stock before deciding to buy or sell. This approach ensures that financial statements reflect real-time value, providing a clearer picture of overall financial health.
net interest marginfinancial
Net interest margin measures how much a bank earns from lending and investing compared with what it pays for funding, expressed as a percentage of its interest-earning assets. Think of it like a grocery store’s markup: it shows the gap between buying cost and selling price per dollar of goods — here, the cost is interest paid and the sale is interest received. Investors watch it because a higher margin usually means a bank is more profitable and better at managing interest rate and credit conditions.
sofrfinancial
The Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) is a market benchmark that measures the cost of borrowing cash overnight using U.S. Treasury securities as collateral. Investors watch SOFR because it acts like a speedometer for short-term interest costs—affecting loan rates, bond yields and the pricing of interest-rate contracts—so movements change borrowing expenses, cash returns and the value of interest-sensitive investments.
allowance for credit lossesfinancial
Allowance for credit losses is a reserve set aside by a financial institution to cover potential losses from borrowers who may not repay their loans. It acts like a safety net, helping the institution prepare for loans that might turn sour. For investors, it signals how cautious the institution is about the quality of its loans and potential risks to its financial health.
initial public offeringfinancial
An initial public offering (IPO) is when a private company first sells its shares to the public and becomes a stock-listed company. It matters because it allows the company to raise money from a wide range of investors, helping it grow, while giving early shareholders a way to sell some of their ownership.

ATLANTA, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MetroCity Bankshares, Inc. ("MetroCity" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: MCBS), holding company for Metro City Bank (the "Bank"), today reported net income of $24.3 million, or $0.84 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $22.1 million, or $0.76 per diluted share, for the second quarter of 2026, and $17.3 million, or $0.67 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $68.7 million or $2.37 per diluted share, compared to $50.4 million, or $1.96 per diluted share, for the same period in 2025.

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights:

  • Annualized return on average assets was 2.12% compared to 1.96% for the second quarter of 2026 and 1.89% for the third quarter of 2025.
  • Annualized return on average equity was 16.97%, compared to 16.01% for the second quarter of 2026 and 15.69% for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted return on average shareholders' equity1, which excluded average accumulated other comprehensive income and merger-related expenses, was 17.04% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 16.17% for the second quarter of 2026, and 16.10% for the third quarter of 2025.
  • Efficiency ratio was 41.81%, compared to 40.08% for the second quarter of 2026 and 38.65% for the third quarter of 2025. Operating efficiency ratio1 was 41.56%, compared to 39.54% for the second quarter of 2026 and 37.85% for the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net interest margin was 4.07%, compared to 4.11% for the second quarter of 2026 and 3.68% for the third quarter of 2025.

Year-to-Date 2026 Highlights:

  • Return on average assets increased to 1.99% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 1.87% for the same period in 2025.
  • Return on average equity increased to 16.54% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 15.70% for the same period in 2025. Adjusted return on average shareholders' equity1, which, excluded average accumulated other comprehensive income and merger-related expenses, was 16.93% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 16.25% for the same period in 2025.
  • Efficiency ratio increased to 41.35% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 38.06% for the same period in 2025.
  • Net interest margin increased by 38 basis points to 4.09% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 3.71% for the same period in 2025.

________________________

Results of Operations

Net Income

Net income was $24.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $2.2 million, or 9.8%, from $22.1 million for the second quarter of 2026. The increase primarily reflected a $4.8 million decrease in income tax expense, including a $4.0 million tax credit benefit, partially offset by a $1.4 million decrease in noninterest income, a $720,000 reduction in the recovery for credit losses, a $483,000 decrease in net interest income, and an $87,000 increase in noninterest expense.  Net income increased by $7.0 million, or 40.7%, compared to $17.3 million for third quarter of 2025.  The year-over-year increase reflected the acquisition of First IC Corporation ("First IC") in the fourth quarter of 2025 and was primarily attributable to a $15.7 million increase in interest income and a decrease in a $2.9 million increase in income tax, offset by a $4.0 million increase in interest expense, a $5.4 million increase in noninterest expenses, a $1.8 million decrease in noninterest income, and a $471,000 reduction in the recovery for credit losses.

Net income was $68.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $18.4 million, or 36.4%, from $50.4 million for same period in 2025. The increase reflected the First IC acquisition in the fourth quarter of 2025, and was primarily attributable to a $37.6 million increase in net interest income and a $1.4 million increase in recovery of credit losses, partially offset by a $18.9 million increase in noninterest expense, an $871,000 decrease in noninterest income and an $885,000 increase in income tax expense.

Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin

Interest income totaled $69.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, down $678,000, or 1.0%, from the previous quarter, primarily due to a $56.2 million decrease in average gross loans. Compared with the third quarter of 2025, interest income increased by $15.7 million, or 29.1%, primarily due to a $766.9 million increase in the average balance of gross loans, a $44.8 million increase in the average balance of investments, and a 33-basis-point increase in loan yield.

Interest expense totaled $26.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $195,000, or 0.7%, from the previous quarter, primarily due to a $27.9 million decrease in average interest-bearing deposits and a $34.8 million decrease in average borrowings. As compared to the third quarter of 2025, interest expense for the third quarter of 2026 increased by $4.0 million, or 17.8%, primarily due to a $562.8 million increase in average interest-bearing deposits balances and offset by a $49.6 million decrease in average borrowing balances and a three-basis point decrease in interest-bearing deposit costs. The Company currently has interest rate derivative agreements totaling $650.0 million that are designated as cash flow hedges of our deposit accounts indexed to the Effective Federal Funds Rate (3.88% as of September 30, 2026). The weighted average pay rate for these interest rate derivatives is 3.38%. During the third quarter of 2026, we recorded a credit to interest expense of $1.5 million from the benefit received on these interest rate derivatives compared to a credit of $1.4 million and $3.8 million recorded during the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025, respectively.

The net interest margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 4.07%, compared to 4.11% for the previous quarter, a decrease of four basis points. The yield on average interest-earning assets decreased by five basis points to 6.52% from 6.57%, while the cost of average interest-bearing liabilities remained unchanged at 3.36%. Average interest-earning assets decreased by $54.1 million from the previous quarter, primarily due to a $56.2 million decrease in average loan balances. Average interest-bearing liabilities decreased by $62.8 million, reflecting a $27.9 million decrease in average interest-bearing deposits and a $34.8 million decrease in average borrowings.

As compared to the same period in 2025, the net interest margin for the third quarter of 2026 increased by 39 basis points to 4.07% from 3.68%, primarily due to a 28-basis-point increase in the yield on average interest-earning assets of $4.24 billion and a six-basis-point decrease in the cost of average interest-bearing liabilities of $3.09 billion. Average earning assets for the third quarter of 2026 increased by $811.7 million from the third quarter of 2025, due to a $44.8 million increase in average total investments and a $766.9 million increase in average loans. Average interest-bearing liabilities for the third quarter of 2026 increased by $513.1 million from the third quarter of 2025, driven by the increase in average interest-bearing deposits of $562.8 million, offset by a $49.6 million decrease in average borrowings.

Noninterest Income

Noninterest income for third quarter of 2026 was $4.4 million, a decrease of $1.4 million, or 23.8%, from the second quarter of 2026, primarily due to lower gain on sale of SBA loans and other income attributable to a decline in the fair value of the equity securities, reflecting changes in market interest rates during the quarter, offset by an increase in SBA servicing income, net and other service charges, commissions and fees.  SBA loan sales totaled $9.7 million (sales premium of 8.16%) during the third quarter of 2026 compared to $27.1 million (sales premium of 8.21%) during the second quarter of 2026. Mortgage loan originations totaled $85.1 million during the third quarter of 2026 compared to $75.4 million during the second quarter of 2026. There were no mortgage loan sales during the third quarter of 2026 or the second quarter of 2026.  During the third quarter of 2026, the fair value of our SBA servicing asset decreased by $218,000 compared to a decrease in fair value of $86,000 during the second quarter of 2026. We also recorded no fair value impairment change on our mortgage servicing asset during the third quarter of 2026 or the second quarter of 2026. The unrealized losses recognized on our equity securities of $743,000.  These equity securities consist of the Company's investment in a mutual fund holding high-quality fixed income securities, which supports affordable housing in the Company's markets and qualifies under the Community Reinvestment Act. Under GAAP, changes in the fair value of this investment are recognized in earnings, even though the underlying holdings are bonds. This investment remains an important part of the Bank's community development strategy, particularly following the completion of our recent merger.

Compared to the third quarter of 2025, noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by $1.8 million or 29.0%, primarily due decreases in servicing income and gain on sale from our residential mortgage loans, servicing income from our SBA loans, other service charges and decline in fair value of equity securities included in other income, offset by increases in gains on sale on SBA loans and service charges on deposit accounts.

Noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $16.5 million, a decrease of $871,000, or 5.0%, from the nine months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to decreases in gain on sale and servicing income on residential mortgage loans, other service charges, and other income, offset by higher gains on sale and servicing income on SBA loans and service charges on deposit accounts.

Noninterest Expense

Noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $20.0 million, an increase of $87,000, or 0.4%, from $20.0 million for the second quarter of 2026. This increase was primarily attributable to increases in salaries and employee benefits, advertising, occupancy and equipment, and data processing, partially offset by a decrease in merger-related expenses and other expenses.

Compared to the third quarter of 2025, noninterest expense during the third quarter of 2026 increased by $5.4 million, or 36.6%, primarily due to higher salaries and employee benefits, occupancy and equipment expense, data processing expense, security expense, loan expense, core deposit amortization expense, and merger-related expenses from the First IC acquisition that occurred in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $61.4 million, an increase of $18.9 million, or 44.3%, from $42.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was primarily attributable to increases in salaries and employee benefits partially due to higher commissions, employee insurance, and stock-based compensation, as well as higher expenses related to merger-related expenses, depreciation, occupancy, data processing, security, loans, and professional services.

The Company's efficiency ratio was 41.81% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 40.08% and 38.65% for the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025, respectively.

Income Tax Expense

The Company's effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 13.1%, compared to 27.7% for the second quarter of 2026 and 27.6% for the third quarter of 2025.  The decrease in effective income tax rate for the quarter was primarily driven by the utilization of tax credits during the current period.

Balance Sheet

Total assets were $4.60 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $77.9 million, or 1.7%, from $4.52 billion at June 30, 2026, and an increase of $968.4 million or 26.7%, from $3.63 billion at September 30, 2025. The $77.9 million increase in total assets at September 30, 2026 compared to June 30, 2026 was primarily due to increases of $50.3 million in cash and cash equivalents and $36.4 million increase in other assets, primarily related increase in income taxes receivable resulting from the utilization of tax credits during the quarter. The increase in liabilities and equity was $72.7 million in deposits and $15.9 million in increase in retained earnings. The $968.4 million increase in total assets at September 30, 2026 compared to September 30, 2025 was primarily due to the First IC acquisition that occurred in the fourth quarter of 2025, with increases in gross loans of $987.0 million, goodwill and core deposit intangible of $67.7 million, securities of $6.9 million, operating lease right-of-use asset of $5.6 million, servicing asset of $3.5 million, and premises and equipment of $8.3 million partially offset by a decrease in interest rate derivatives of $5.2 million.

Investment Securities

Our investment securities portfolio made up only 0.89% of our total assets at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.99% and 0.94% at June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.

Loans

Gross loans held for investment were $3.98 billion at September 30, 2026, a decrease of $3.8 million, or 0.1%, compared to $3.98 billion at June 30, 2026, and an increase of $1.00 billion, or 33.8%, compared to $2.97 billion at September 30, 2025. The decrease in loans at September 30, 2026 compared to June 30, 2026 was due to a $28.7 million decrease in residential real estate loans, a $3.3 million decrease in commercial and industrial loans, offset by a $16.0 million increase in commercial real estate, and a $12.3 million increase in construction and development loans.  Loans classified as held for sale totaled $0, $1.4 million, and $231.3 million at September 30, 2026, June 30, 2026, and September 30, 2025, respectively.

Deposits

Deposits were $3.56 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $72.7 million, or 2.1%, compared to total deposits of $3.49 billion at June 30, 2026, and an increase of $869.0 million, or 32.3%, compared to total deposits of $2.69 billion at September 30, 2025. The increase in total deposits at September 30, 2026 compared to June 30, 2026 was due to a $45.3 million increase in noninterest-bearing deposits, a $6.6 million increase in time deposits, an $18.6 million increase in money market accounts, and an increase of $2.8 million in interest-bearing demand deposits offset by a $566,000 decrease in savings accounts.

Noninterest-bearing deposits were $828.3 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $783.0 million at June 30, 2026 and $544.4 million at September 30, 2025. Noninterest-bearing deposits constituted 23.3% of total deposits at September 30, 2026, compared to 22.4% at June 30, 2026 and 20.2% at September 30, 2025. Interest-bearing deposits were $2.73 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $2.71 billion at June 30, 2026 and $2.15 billion at September 30, 2025. Interest-bearing deposits constituted 76.7% of total deposits at September 30, 2026, compared to 77.6% at June 30, 2026 and 79.8% at September 30, 2025.

Uninsured deposits were 34.7% of total deposits at September 30, 2026, compared to 33.1% and 26.1% at June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively. As of September 30, 2026, we had a $1.66 billion available borrowing capacity consisting of $964.7 million at the Federal Home Loan Bank, $629.5 million at the Federal Reserve Discount Window, and $67.5 million under fed funds lines with various other financial institutions.

Asset Quality

The Company recorded a recovery for credit losses of $72,000 during the third quarter of 2026, compared to recoveries of $792,000 during the second quarter of 2026 and $543,000 during the third quarter of 2025. The third-quarter recovery primarily reflected lower loan balances. Annualized net recoveries to average loans were 0.00% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to recoveries of 0.01% for the second quarter of 2026 and net charge-offs of 0.03% for the third quarter of 2025.

Nonperforming assets totaled $20.6 million, or 0.45% of total assets, at September 30, 2026 (which comprised of $16.1 million in nonperforming loans and $4.5 million in other real estate owned, including $3.4 million of branches taken out of service) a decrease of $3.2 million, from $23.8 million, of 0.53% of total assets, at June 30, 2026, and an increase of $6.7 million from $14.0 million, or 0.38% of total assets, at September 30, 2025.  The decrease in nonperforming assets at September 30, 2026 compared to June 30, 2026 was due to a $6.4 million decrease in nonperforming loans offset by an increase in other real estate owned of $3.2 million.

Allowance for credit losses as a percentage of total loans was 0.65% at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.65% at June 30, 2026 and 0.60% at September 30, 2025. Allowance for credit losses as a percentage of nonperforming loans was 159.78% at September 30, 2026, compared to 114.63% and 137.66% at June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.

SEC registration enables Cboe Clear U.S. to clear binary securities options alongside futures, positioning it to support innovation across the market

CHICAGO, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe: CBOE), a leading global markets operator and pioneer in equity and index derivatives, today announced that Cboe Clear U.S., LLC (CCUS) has received temporary registration from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to operate as a Covered Clearing Agency.

The registration expands CCUS's clearing capabilities beyond its existing authorities as a Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)-registered Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) to clear securities products in addition to futures and swaps products. Together with recent enhancements to its regulatory framework and product scope, the milestone positions CCUS to support innovation and emerging opportunities across a broad range of assets and markets.

CCUS will initially use its SEC registration to clear Cboe's binary securities options tied to specified corporate key performance indicators (KPIs), which are planned to list on Cboe Options Exchange and be available on Robinhood in the fourth-quarter 2026. CCUS also recently received CFTC approval to clear margined futures broadly and continues to clear digital asset derivatives under its DCO designation.

"Clearing plays a critical role in bringing innovation to market," said Dale Michaels, Head of Cboe Clear U.S. "These expanded capabilities position Cboe Clear U.S. to become an innovation lane to support new products and meet evolving customer needs, while maintaining the rigorous risk management standards that are fundamental to our business."

These efforts complement Cboe's longstanding partnership with The Options Clearing Corporation (OCC)® and Cboe's continued commitment to supporting the established clearing infrastructure for traditional equity options.

The development builds on the growth of Cboe's established European clearing business, where Cboe Clear Europe has become the leading pan-European equities central counterparty, while expanding into new services such as securities financing transaction clearing. Together, these advances demonstrate Cboe's ability to extend its clearing capabilities across markets and asset classes.

To support its own future growth, CCUS has strengthened its infrastructure over the past year, including electing in June to become a Subpart C DCO. In doing so, CCUS is voluntarily adopting the enhanced standards the CFTC applies to systemically important DCOs for financial resources, risk management and operational resilience, aligning with those applied to leading global clearing organizations.

About Cboe Global Markets

Cboe Global Markets (Cboe: CBOE) is a leading global markets operator with a long history of innovation in equity and index derivatives. Since launching the world's first listed options exchange in 1973, Cboe has pioneered landmark products, including the introduction of S&P 500® index options and the creation of the VIX® Index, the world's leading gauge of market volatility, reshaping how investors manage risk and access opportunity. Paige Spiranac and Team Grass League claimed golf’s orangest jacket following a dramatic comeback victory, with Flo Rida bringing the two-day event to an electrifying close with a hit-filled performance

RICHMOND, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Helix Innovations LLC, an operating company of Altria Group, Inc. (Altria) (NYSE: MO), today announced the winners of on!® nicotine pouches’ inaugural on!vitational, held October 16 and 17 at TGL’s SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida. The two-day golf and entertainment experience brought together eight teams of current and former professional athletes, golf personalities, entertainers and adult nicotine consumers age 25+ for a competition that combined golf, technology and entertainment.

Well-known golf influencer Paige Spiranac and Team Grass League, including former professional golfer Drew Kittleson and Grass League co-founder Jimmy Hoselton, captured the inaugural on!vitational Championship. The team defeated former PGA TOUR veteran Ricky Barnes and Team Troon in a dramatic final to claim the tournament trophy and golf’s orangest jacket. After teams including Malbon, Palm Tree Crew and Hypegolf battled throughout the competition, Grass League staged a thrilling comeback, with an on!® consumer sweepstakes winner delivering a pivotal shot on the penultimate hole to help secure the victory.

Unlike traditional golf tournaments, the on!vitational put nicotine consumers 25+ directly into the competition alongside some of the biggest personalities in golf, sports and entertainment. Consumer participants, selected at random through an on!® sweepstakes earlier this year, competed as members of the eight teams. The two-day event was emceed by popular golf influencer and TGL host Roger Steele.

Grass League co-founder Jimmy Hoselton summed up the excitement: “on!® has been with us from the beginning. We're all in on on!®, and we're all in on the on!vitational.”

A New Kind of Golf Competition

Held inside TGL’s 250,000-square-foot SoFi Center, the on!vitational took advantage of the venue’s technology, including its over four-story tall simulator screen and real-life putting and short-game areas, to deliver a golf experience unlike a traditional tournament.

The competition also featured unique in-match opportunities. Momentum Swing allowed the sweepstakes winners to chip into designated round spots on the green for significant bonus points while Celeb Shot allowed teams to choose any team member to take a shot, regardless of whose turn it was. All Axis offered a strategic element where teams could move the green 45 or 90 degrees in any direction after their opponent was on or close to the green to gain short game and putting advantages at key moments.

These elements ended up being major factors in the final. Grass League was down 6-0 on No. 6. They used their Celeb Shot to allow Kittleson to hit, and he delivered. He chipped it in from off the green to give Grass League their first points of the match. A 20-foot birdie putt on No. 7 by Hoselton pulled Team Grass League within two points, and the Momentum Swing was the deciding factor. Trailing 6-4 on No. 8, Team Grass League sweepstakes winner William K. chipped it into one of the designated spots, scoring six points, and clinching the comeback Championship victory.

"This was one of the best experiences of my life," said on!® sweepstakes and Team Grass League winner William K. in a post-match interview. "My team kept picking me up throughout the tournament, and I was able to deliver when it counted. Really thankful to on!® for putting on such a great event."

Beyond the competition, multi-platinum recording artist Flo Rida headlined Saturday's entertainment, bringing an energy-filled conclusion to two great days of golf. He performed some of his biggest hits and invited tournament winners and guests to join him onstage.

Honoring Veterans Through Golf

The on!vitational also featured a partnership with the Veteran Golfers Association (VGA), a nonprofit dedicated to enriching the lives of veterans and their family members through the camaraderie and sportsmanship of golf.

In addition to competing as one of the tournament's eight teams, the VGA participated in a special military salute recognizing U.S. Navy veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Edward C. Byers Jr., who attended the event. All proceeds from can sales at the on!vitational went towards supporting the VGA and its mission.

Relive the on!vitational

Fans 21 or older can relive the competition, winning moments, player highlights and entertainment through content available on the on!® Instagram.

About on!® Nicotine Pouches

on!® and on! PLUS® nicotine pouches are designed for adult nicotine consumers 21+ looking for a satisfying, premium nicotine pouch experience. With six varieties and three nicotine strengths, on!® nicotine pouches deliver against a wide variety of adult consumer 21+ tastes and preferences. on! PLUS® nicotine pouches are designed with a proprietary NICOSILK™ mesh technology for a comfortable feel. on! PLUS® is available in Mint, Wintergreen & Tobacco flavors at 6, 9 and 12 mg strengths. on! PLUS® will also offer the same three strength options in exciting new flavors: Blueberry Mint, Mango Pineapple and Watermelon Mint (select stores only).

Helix Innovations LLC Profile

Helix Innovations LLC (Helix), an Altria company, offers a portfolio of oral nicotine pouch products for adult nicotine consumers 21+, including on!® and on! PLUS®. In December 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration authorized the marketing of certain on! PLUS® variants.

Helix is committed to responsible marketing and preventing underage access to nicotine products. As an Altria operating company, Helix follows marketing practices designed to appeal to adult nicotine consumers 21+ while taking steps to limit reach to underage audiences.

No one under the age of 21 should use nicotine products. Nicotine is addictive, and nicotine products are not risk-free. on!® products are intended for adult nicotine consumers 21+.

LUND, Sweden, October 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hansa Biopharma AB, "Hansa" (Nasdaq Stockholm: HNSA), today announced that data from the European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study of Idefirix® (imlifidase) were presented during the High-Impact Clinical Trials oral session at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The abstract "FR-OR103 Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES): An Open-Label Post-Authorization Trial of 50 Imlifidase Crossmatch-Positive Deceased-Donor Kidney Transplants in Europe" was selected as a Late-Breaking Abstract at the congress.

Renée Aguiar-Lucander, CEO of Hansa Biopharma, said: "The presentation of the PAES study in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session highlights the scientific and clinical relevance of these findings and the potential of imlifidase to address a significant unmet need for highly sensitized patients awaiting kidney transplantation. We are encouraged by the continued interest from the transplant community in the growing body of evidence supporting imlifidase."

Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain and investigator for the trial said: "The successful completion of the PAES study provides important evidence in a patient population that continues to face significant challenges in accessing kidney transplantation. These findings add to the clinical evidence supporting the use of imlifidase to enable transplantation in highly sensitized patients with a positive crossmatch against a deceased donor."

ASN Kidney Week is one of the world's leading scientific meetings in nephrology and transplantation, bringing together researchers and clinicians to present the latest advances in kidney disease and transplantation medicine. The High-Impact Clinical Trials session features selected studies considered to represent some of the most clinically relevant and impactful research presented at the congress.

The abstract was presented by Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain, on behalf of the PAES study investigators.

Summary of the Abstract

Background

Imlifidase have a conditional approval in Europe since 2020. PAES (NCT05369975) is a controlled, non-randomized, open-label post-authorization efficacy and safety trial, designed to provide comprehensive data to support a full marketing authorisation of imlifidase (Idefirix®) in Europe.

Methods

Fifty highly sensitized (HS) patients who received crossmatch positive kidney offers received imlifidase treatment in line with the mode-of-action i.e. conversion of a positive crossmatch to a negative crossmatch and thereby enabling transplantation. All patients were unlikely to be transplanted under available kidney allocation systems, including prioritization programs for HS patients.

The primary trial objective was to assess graft failure-free survival at 1 year after transplantation. Secondary outcomes at 1 year includes kidney function assessed by eGFR, patient survival, graft survival, delayed graft function (DGF), antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) and safety.

Results

  • The graft failure-free survival was 90% at 1 year after transplantation in patients desensitized with imlifidase (n=50).
  • Graft and patient survival were 92% and 98%, respectively.
  • The mean eGFR calculated by MDRD was 51.04 mL/min/1.73 m2 (n=45).
  • DGF was seen in 40% of patients with a median duration of 14 days.
  • AMR occurred in 56% of recipients; however, no allograft loss was associated with AMR.
  • There were no new or additional safety signals found, and no imlifidase infusions were stopped due to infusion reactions.

Conclusion

Imlifidase enables kidney transplantation with a successful kidney function measured as eGFR at 1 year in patients desensitized. Imlifidase was well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with prior experience and no unexpected or unacceptable risks observed.

Information about the trial is available at ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05369975

Notes to editors

About highly sensitized patients

Highly sensitized patients have pre-formed antibodies with a broad reactivity against human leukocyte antigens (HLAs). Those antibodies can cause damage to a transplanted organ and potentially graft loss.1 The presence of HLA antibodies means that highly sensitized patients have limited or no access to transplantation, as finding a compatible donor organ 

is particularly challenging.2,3 The immunological complexity of highly sensitized patients make them spend a longer time on transplant waiting lists, with an increased risk of dying while waiting for a suitable donor organ.4,5 Across the U.S. and Europe, highly sensitized patients comprise around 10-15% of all patients on transplant waiting lists.6,7

About Idefirix® (imlifidase)

Imlifidase is an antibody-cleaving enzyme originating from Streptococcus pyogenes that specifically cleaves and inactivates all immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody subclasses, including HLAs. It has a rapid onset and inactivates IgG-antibodies within hours after administration. The decrease in antibody levels creates a temporal antibody-free window of opportunity for highly sensitised patients to undergo transplant, thus enabling successful transplantation from an otherwise incompatible donor.

Imlifidase received a conditional marketing authorization valid throughout the European Union on 25 August 2020 and is marketed under the trade name Idefirix for the desensitization treatment of highly sensitized adult kidney transplant patients with a positive crossmatch against an available deceased donor. The use of Idefirix should be reserved for patients who are unlikely to be transplanted under the available kidney allocation system, including prioritization programs for highly sensitized patients.

The efficacy and safety of imlifidase as a pre-transplant treatment to reduce donor-specific IgG antibodies was studied in four phase 2 single-arm, studies in EU and US, a controlled Phase 3 study in US and in this European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study. 5,7,10-11 .

Full EU product information can be accessed via the initial Summary of Product Characteristics found here

Idefirix is exclusively out-licensed for transplantation in EU, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Iceland and Middle East and North Africa (MENA) to SERB Pharmaceuticals since July 1, 2026.

In the US, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted the Biologics License Application (BLA) for imlifidase in February of 2026 and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) action date of December 19, 2026.

About kidney failure

Kidney disease can progress to kidney failure or End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), identified when a patient's kidney function is less than 15%.12 ESRD poses a significant health burden, affecting nearly 2.5 million patients worldwide.12 A kidney transplant is the treatment of choice for suitable patients with ESRD because it offers improved survival and quality of life benefits, and is cost savings compared to long-term dialysis. There are approximately 170,000 kidney patients in the U.S. and Europe waiting for a new kidney.13

Hansa Biopharma AB is a pioneering commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing and commercializing novel immunomodulatory therapies to transform care for patients with acute or complex immune disorders. Hansa's proprietary IgG-cleaving enzyme technology platform addresses serious unmet medical needs in transplantation, gene therapy and autoimmune diseases. The company's portfolio includes imlifidase, a first-in-class immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody-cleaving enzyme therapy, which has been shown to enable kidney transplantation in highly sensitized patients, and HNSA-5487, a next-generation IgG-cleaving molecule that will be developed for Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS). data.description:
The new regimen allows patients to begin SKYRIZI treatment at home rather than starting with intravenous administration.

Add on Google
  • Now with a new route of induction administration, subcutaneous SKYRIZI supports early symptomatic and endoscopic control with an on-body injector (OBI) device throughout the course of treatment
  • In the pivotal Phase 3 AFFIRM study, subcutaneous (SC) SKYRIZI® achieved superior clinical remissioni and endoscopic responseii at week 12 compared with placebo in patients with Crohn's disease; results were particularly strong in patients without prior advanced therapy failureiii
  • The safety profile of subcutaneous induction was generally consistent with the established SKYRIZI profile in Crohn's disease, with no new safety risks identified
  • FDA also approved an update to the U.S. Prescribing Information warning and precautions across all indications to allow healthcare providers to use clinical judgment when determining whether tuberculosis (TB) testing is needed

NORTH CHICAGO, Ill., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a subcutaneous (SC) induction regimen for SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) for adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease (CD)iv. Patients now have the option to start SKYRIZI treatment at home, with induction doses delivered by an on-body injector (OBI) induction pack and then continue using an OBI once every eight weeks throughout the course of maintenance treatment.

"People living with Crohn's disease need treatments that can deliver meaningful disease control from the start," said Roopal Thakkar, M.D., executive vice president, research and development, chief scientific officer, AbbVie. "With the approval of subcutaneous induction, we are building on the strong efficacy of SKYRIZI while giving patients and physicians greater flexibility in how treatment is initiated. This is one more example of how AbbVie continues to advance treatment to better meet the needs of people living with Crohn's disease."

Subcutaneous SKYRIZI Shows High Rates of Clinical Remission and Endoscopic Response by Week 12iii 
This FDA approval is supported by positive results from the Phase 3 AFFIRM trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of SC SKYRIZI versus placebo in patients with moderately to severely active CD.iii SKYRIZI achieved superiority of the co-primary endpoints of clinical remission and endoscopic response at week 12.iii Although the study enrolled a primarily treatment-refractory population, these Phase 3 results were particularly strong within patients without prior advanced therapy failure (advanced therapy-naïve).iii By week 12, nearly three-quarters (74%) of advanced therapy (AT)-naïve patients were in clinical remission (vs. 27% placebo) and these AT-naïve patients achieved endoscopic response at four times the rate of placebo (60% vs. 15%, respectively).iii SC SKYRIZI also had a higher efficacy response in patients who had previously failed advanced therapy.iii

SC SKYRIZI also met secondary endpoints including endoscopic remission and FACIT fatigue scores at week 12 vs. placebo.iii The safety profile of SC SKYRIZI for induction was generally consistent with its known profile in CD, with no new safety risks observed.iii

Together, these results demonstrate market-leading clinical and endoscopic outcomes in advanced therapy-naïve patients that set a high bar in CD. Furthermore, the strength of these subcutaneous results provides a compelling foundation for future clinical trials.

Subcutaneous Treatment With SKYRIZI Offers Fully Self-Administered Therapy From the Start 
The induction dosing regimen with SC SKYRIZI is 720 mg delivered by OBI induction pack at weeks 0, 2, 4 and 8.iii Patients also have the option to start treatment intravenously with 600 mg delivered at weeks 0, 4 and 8.iii Patients can then continue with maintenance dosing starting at week 12 administered by OBI every eight weeks.iii

"When patients and I discuss treatment, they want to know two things: will it work? And how will it fit into their lives?" said Millie D. Long, M.D., MPH, chief, division of gastroenterology and hepatology, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and lead investigator of AFFIRM. "AFFIRM answered the first question, with superior rates of clinical remission and endoscopic response versus placebo during induction with subcutaneous SKYRIZI, particularly in patients new to advanced therapy. This approval answers the second. As a physician who has used the SKYRIZI OBI, I've seen firsthand the convenience it can offer patients. Now with this approval, patients can start treatment at home and continue the same way through maintenance."

Patients Report Satisfaction and Ease of Use in Real World Experience With SKYRIZI OBI
First introduced in 2022 for CD maintenance treatment, the SKYRIZI OBI has demonstrated strong user experience. In a real-world survey of 186 people living with CD, 88% reported AbbVie's OBI easy to use.v In evaluating alternative routes of administration, a patient-reported survey of 352 adults living with IBD found 87% were satisfied or highly satisfied with OBI compared to 71% with an autoinjectorvi, demonstrating patient preference for OBI.

FDA Also Approved Update to Tuberculosis (TB) Language in U.S. Prescribing Information
Additionally, the FDA approved an update to the SKYRIZI prescribing information's warning and precautions language across all approved indications.iii The revised label advises healthcare providers to consider TB evaluation prior to treatment initiation based on clinical judgment.iii This change gives healthcare providers greater flexibility in patient assessment before starting SKYRIZI treatment. There is no mandatory TB test prior to initiating SKYRIZI.

About Crohn's Disease 
Crohn's disease is a chronic, systemic disease that manifests as inflammation within the gastrointestinal tract, most commonly in the area between the small intestine (ileum) and the colon, causing persistent diarrhea and abdominal pain.vii,viii It is a progressive disease, meaning it gets worse over time and may lead to life-threatening complications or surgery.ix,x Because the signs and symptoms of Crohn's disease are unpredictable, it causes a significant burden on people living with the disease—not only physically but also emotionally and economically.xi

About the AFFIRM Studyxii
AFFIRM is a global, Phase 3, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of risankizumab subcutaneous (SC) as an induction treatment in adult patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease. Co-primary endpoints were percentage of participants with CDAI Clinical Remission (CDAI < 150) and percentage of participants with endoscopic response at week 12. A total of 274 patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to risankizumab SC or placebo. Key demographics and baseline characteristics were generally balanced between the risankizumab SC and placebo groups; 65% had failed advanced therapies for the treatment of CD before. The study consists of three treatment periods: a placebo-controlled Period A (baseline to week 12) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of risankizumab SC induction treatment, an extended Period B (week 12 to 24) where patients receive blinded or open-label treatments based on their clinical response at week 12, and a 52-week open-label extension Period C where all patients receive the approved risankizumab maintenance treatment.xii More information on this trial can be found at www.clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06063967).xii

Patient Access and Support
AbbVie is committed to helping people access SKYRIZI and other medicines, including offering a patient support program and co-pay card that may reduce out-of-pocket costs to as little as $0 per month for eligible, commercially insured patients. For those with limited or no health insurance, AbbVie offers myAbbVie Assist, a patient assistance program that provides SKYRIZI at no charge to those who qualify. More information about this assistance program can be found at www.AbbVie.com/myAbbVieAssist.

About SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa)
SKYRIZI is an interleukin-23 (IL-23) inhibitor that blocks IL-23 by selectively binding to its p19 subunit. IL-23, a cytokine involved in inflammatory processes, is thought to be linked to a number of chronic immune-mediated diseases.iii SKYRIZI is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and Crohn's disease.iii

SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) U.S. Uses and Important Safety Informationiii
SKYRIZI is a prescription medicine used to treat:

  • moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and children 6 years of age and older who may benefit from taking injections or pills (systemic therapy) or treatment using ultraviolet or UV light (phototherapy).
  • active psoriatic arthritis in adults and children 6 years of age and older.
  • moderately to severely active Crohn's disease in adults.
  • moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adults.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa)?

SKYRIZI is a prescription medicine that may cause serious side effects, including:

Serious allergic reactions:

  • Stop using SKYRIZI and get emergency medical help right away if you get any of the following symptoms of a serious allergic reaction:
    • fainting, dizziness, feeling lightheaded (low blood pressure)
    • swelling of your face, eyelids, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat
    • trouble breathing or throat tightness
    • chest tightness
    • skin rash, hives
    • itching

Infections:
SKYRIZI may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections. Your healthcare provider may check you for infections and tuberculosis (TB) before starting treatment with SKYRIZI and may treat you for TB before you begin treatment with SKYRIZI if you have a history of TB or have active TB. Your healthcare provider should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during and after treatment with SKYRIZI.

  • Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have an infection or have symptoms of an infection, including:
    • fever, sweats, or chills
    • cough
    • shortness of breath
    • blood in your mucus (phlegm)
    • muscle aches
    • warm, red, or painful skin or sores on your body different from your psoriasis
    • weight loss
    • diarrhea or stomach pain
    • burning when you urinate or urinating more often than normal

Do not use SKYRIZI if you are allergic to risankizumab-rzaa or any of the ingredients in SKYRIZI. See the Medication Guide or Consumer Brief Summary for a complete list of ingredients.

Before using SKYRIZI, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

  • have any of the conditions or symptoms listed in the section "What is the most important information I should know about SKYRIZI?"
  • have an infection that does not go away or that keeps coming back.
  • have TB or have been in close contact with someone with TB.
  • have recently received or are scheduled to receive an immunization (vaccine). Medications that interact with the immune system may increase your risk of getting an infection after receiving live vaccines. You should avoid receiving live vaccines right before, during, or right after treatment with SKYRIZI. Tell your healthcare provider that you are taking SKYRIZI before receiving a vaccine.
  • are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known if SKYRIZI can harm your unborn baby.
  • are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if SKYRIZI passes into your breast milk.
  • become pregnant while taking SKYRIZI. You are encouraged to enroll in the Pregnancy Registry, which is used to collect information about the health of you and your baby. Talk to your healthcare provider or call 1-877-302-2161 or visit http://glowpregnancyregistry.com to enroll in this registry.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.

What are the possible side effects of SKYRIZI?

SKYRIZI may cause serious side effects. See "What is the most important information I should know about SKYRIZI?"

Liver problems may happen while being treated for Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis: A person with Crohn's disease who received SKYRIZI through a vein in the arm developed changes in liver blood tests with a rash that led to hospitalization. Your healthcare provider will do blood tests to check your liver before, during, and at least up to 12 weeks of treatment, and may stop treatment with SKYRIZI if you develop liver problems. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you notice any of the following symptoms: unexplained rash, nausea, vomiting, stomach (abdominal) pain, tiredness (fatigue), loss of appetite, yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice), and dark urine.

The most common side effects of SKYRIZI in people treated for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis include: upper respiratory infections, headache, joint pain, stomach (abdominal) pain, injection site reactions, low red blood cells (anemia), fever, back pain, urinary tract infection, and rash.

The most common side effects of SKYRIZI in people treated for plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis include: upper respiratory infections, headache, feeling tired, injection site reactions, and fungal skin infections.

These are not all the possible side effects of SKYRIZI. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

Use SKYRIZI exactly as your healthcare provider tells you to use it.

SKYRIZI (risankizumab-rzaa) is available in a 150 mg/mL prefilled syringe and pen, a 55 mg/0.37 mL prefilled syringe, a 600 mg/10 mL vial for intravenous infusion, and a 180 mg/1.2 mL or 360 mg/2.4 mL single-dose prefilled cartridge with on-body injector.
